expectations.text: Describes six cans
I can tithe can at 10% of gross
I can finish free can: 10%, never spent, used to buy income-producing assets / passive income
I can educate myself can at 10% for seminars, books, audio
I can save for what I want and I can have fun (spend every month) cans
expectations.evidence: Save for what I want; have fun spent monthly

expectations.text: I can pay my bills can at 50% for living expenses
Four panes: Have A Job (H.A.J.), Own A Job (O.A.J.), Sow Money Seeds (S.M.S.), Own A System (O.A.S.)
Have/own a job are the two worst ways; Own A System best; Sow Money Seeds second best
Financial house windows: income, outgo, wealth reducing liabilities, income producing assets
Poor: all income goes out the outgo window
Middle class: buy wealth reducing liabilities / live in debt keeping up with the Joneses
Rich: buy income producing assets; difference is what you do with money, not how much you make
expectations.evidence: Rich IPAs; what you do with money

expectations.text: Lists several of the 11 mental money traps (e.g., negativism for skepticism, value security over freedom, renter's mentality, technophobic, formal over self-education)
Lists several practical traps (e.g., paralyzed by a paycheck, don't invest in greatest asset, no financial mentor, bad debt, do everything themselves)
Hands-free plan: home business to $10,000/month within two years with minimal ('one finger') effort, then start another
Prefers product-oriented over service business (time limits income)
Mentions virtual millionaire (V.M.) vs V.P. and/or 'you're in the marketing business'
Notes caveats such as due diligence / results not guaranteed
